title: Manchester United’s JJ Gabriel a ‘big talent’ but ‘too young’ to make matchday squad – Michael Carrick
content:
Michael Carrick has reminded Manchester United fans of the legal considerations regarding young forward JJ Gabriel’s playing future.

Gabriel, 15, has 20 goals in 22 appearances across the under-18 academy competitions this season. A talented and well-regarded prospect within United’s academy, the teenager is unable to feature in U21 or senior team matchday squads on account of his young age.

“He’s not allowed,” said Carrick when asked if he had considered featuring the young forward in a matchday squad. “He’s too young.”

Gabriel is unable to feature in matchday squads higher than under-18 level because he was 14 years of age when the 2025-26 season began. Premier League rules allow a 15-year-old to play so long as they are 15 by August 31 of the campaign in question.

Nominally a winger, the teenager has been afforded more opportunities in central areas in recent matches in an attempt to further his development and better acclimatise him to the more physical elements of the game in congested spaces. He has also featured for England’s under-15 and under-16 sides.

Speaking before facing Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, Carrick described Gabriel – who celebrated his 15th birthday in October – as a “big talent” and a player for the future.

“We’ve got some really good young players in the academy, and we try and get the younger players up as much as we can,” said the interim head coach.

“JJ’s a big talent. It’s pretty obvious to know that. And he’s had a really good season for the under-18s. We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with working with him, as we do with all the different age groups and younger players.

Picking the right moment to step up, picking the right moment to leave them in a certain place and (other) ups and downs. But he’s done well in his training, he’s done well, as you’d expect. It’s good to have the younger players come up with us.”

Arsenal’s Ethan Nwaneri became the youngest ever Premier League player when he came on as a late substitute against Brentford in September 2022, aged 15 and 181 days. Fellow Arsenal teenager Max Dowman became the second youngest-ever player in the competition when he played against Leeds United in August 2025, aged 15 years and 235 days.

Angel Gomes is United’s youngest-ever Premier League player after his debut in May 2017, aged 16 years and 263 days.

Gabriel is likely to feature for United’s under-18 side in their FA Youth Cup quarter-final against Sunderland on March 18. The fixture will be played at Old Trafford on Wednesday.
